born.name: Christian Doppler
born.short: Gave his name to the Doppler effect
bio: Born in Salzburg, Austria, the son of a stonemason, he was too frail for the family trade and turned to mathematics instead.
In 1842 he explained why a sound or light changes pitch as its source moves towards us or away from us – the Doppler effect.
Every passing ambulance siren proves him right, and his idea now helps astronomers, weather forecasters and hospital scanners.

born.name: Louisa May Alcott
bio: Raised in Concord, Massachusetts, she wrote from a young age to help support her hard-up family.
Little Women, published in 1868, drew on her own life with her three sisters and became an instant success.
Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy have never been out of print, and their story has been filmed and staged many times over.

born.name: Gertrude Jekyll
born.short: The queen of the English cottage border
bio: Born in London and raised in Surrey, she trained as an artist before failing eyesight turned her towards gardening.
She designed some four hundred gardens, many alongside the architect Edwin Lutyens, and wrote books still read today.
Her soft, painterly borders shaped the look of the English garden – and her home at Munstead Wood is now cared for by the National Trust.

born.name: C. S. Lewis
bio: Born in Belfast, Clive Staples Lewis – “Jack” to his friends – became an Oxford don and a close friend of J. R. R. Tolkien.
The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe appeared in 1950, the first of seven Chronicles of Narnia.
The books have sold more than 100 million copies, and generations of children have checked the backs of wardrobes ever since.

born.name: John Mayall
bio: Born in Macclesfield, Cheshire, he formed John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers in the early 1960s.
The band was a finishing school for future stars, including Eric Clapton, Peter Green, John McVie and Mick Taylor.
He kept touring well into his eighties and was voted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2024, the year he died, aged 90.

born.name: Gemma Chan
bio: Born in London, she studied law at Oxford but turned down a legal career to go to drama school instead.
She won British fans as the android Mia in Channel 4’s Humans, then found worldwide fame in Crazy Rich Asians.
Her films since include Captain Marvel, Eternals and Don’t Worry Darling.

remembered.name: Mary Somerville
remembered.short: The Scot who explained the heavens
bio: Largely self-taught, she studied mathematics in secret as a girl in Burntisland, Fife, when it was thought unsuitable for women.
Her books on astronomy and physics were bestsellers, and she was one of the first two women elected to the Royal Astronomical Society.
Somerville College, Oxford, is named after her, and she appears on the Royal Bank of Scotland’s £10 note.

remembered.name: Giacomo Puccini
bio: Born in Lucca into a long line of church musicians, he decided to write opera after seeing Verdi’s Aida.
La Bohème, Tosca and Madama Butterfly made him the most popular opera composer of his day.
He died before finishing Turandot, whose aria Nessun dorma later became a football anthem at Italia ’90.

remembered.name: Cary Grant
bio: Born Archibald Leach in Bristol, he left school to join a troupe of acrobats and sailed with them to America.
He became Hollywood’s ultimate gentleman in films such as The Philadelphia Story, North by Northwest and To Catch a Thief.
Effortlessly charming on screen, he once said: everybody wants to be Cary Grant – even I want to be Cary Grant.

remembered.name: George Harrison
bio: Born in Liverpool, he joined the Quarrymen as a teenager and became lead guitarist of The Beatles.
He wrote Something, Here Comes the Sun and While My Guitar Gently Weeps, and introduced Western pop to the sitar.
His solo album All Things Must Pass was a triumph, and in 1971 he staged the Concert for Bangladesh.

history.head: Over the South Pole
history.body: American explorer Richard Byrd and his crew, with Norwegian Bernt Balchen at the controls, make the first flight over the South Pole.

history.head: A chimp in orbit
history.body: Enos the chimpanzee is launched by NASA and circles the Earth twice, paving the way for John Glenn’s flight.

history.head: Beatlemania
history.body: The Beatles release I Want to Hold Your Hand in Britain, with around a million copies ordered in advance.

history.head: Game on
history.body: Atari releases Pong, the simple electronic tennis game that launched the video games industry.

uk: When You’re in Love with a Beautiful Woman

sport.head: Barça is born
sport.body: Swiss businessman Joan Gamper and a group of football lovers found FC Barcelona at a gymnasium in the city.

sport.head: Football on the wireless
sport.body: The Chicago Bears beat the Detroit Lions 19–16 in the first NFL game broadcast across America on radio.

sport.head: Murray’s Davis Cup
sport.body: Andy Murray beats David Goffin in Ghent to give Great Britain its first Davis Cup title since 1936.

sport.head: Messi’s magnificent seven
sport.body: Lionel Messi wins a record seventh Ballon d’Or at a ceremony in Paris.
